headline: Cancel pairs of different values
statement: Return the value occurring more than floor(n/2) times in nums. The input is nonempty and a majority element is guaranteed.
intuition: Imagine canceling a pair of different values whenever possible. A value appearing more than half the time cannot be completely canceled. Keep one candidate and a balance of unmatched votes. Change the candidate only when the balance reaches zero.
approach: Keep a candidate and a vote balance.
When balance is zero, choose the current value as candidate.
Add one for a candidate match, subtract one for a different value.
Return the surviving candidate; no verification pass is needed under the guarantee.
correctness: Removing a pair of different values preserves the strict-majority identity: the majority loses at most one occurrence while two elements disappear. The vote algorithm performs these cancellations implicitly. Since a majority exists, the uncancelled candidate must be that value.
bruteForce: Count each distinct value by scanning nums: O(n²) worst case. A frequency map costs O(n) space.

complexity.explanation: Time O(n); additional space O(1). Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: The guarantee is essential; arbitrary arrays need a second verification pass.
Reset the candidate when the balance is zero, before updating the vote.
Majority means more than half, not just most frequent.
